A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same scRatio research work. Their main text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices are readable and support reliable comparison.

before.justification: V1 reports original Gaussian density-ratio and mutual-information experiments, semi-synthetic differential-abundance results, and single-cell biological case studies.

after.justification: V2 retains original experimental results and reports additional classifier comparisons and numerical reliability ablations.

M1.justification: The density-ratio ODE, S1/S2 simulation fields, flow schedules, separate score and velocity networks, and Algorithm 1 are retained. New theory and ablations analyze existing choices without changing the proposed procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same Gaussian tasks, PBMC68k, NeurIPS 2021, C. elegans, ComboSciPlex, and donor-cytokine data. The low-overlap Gaussian setting with shift 4 already appears in v1's appendix. New ablations vary training and model settings within retained coverage.

E2.justification: V2 adds an MLP classifier/log-odds comparator to mutual-information estimation in Table 1 and Gaussian ratio estimation in Figure 8. Existing flow-based and time-score comparators, plus MrVI and MELD for differential abundance, remain.

E3.justification: V1 fixes the TSM/CTSM SB noise parameter at 1; v2 reports learning-rate and path-variance searches with validation-based selection. MI evaluation also switches from analytic reference values, approximately 5.11–81.73, to 5, 10, 20, 40, and 80 in Table 6. New ablations introduce sample-size sweeps and crossed training checkpoints with identity encoders.

E4.justification: V2 adds sample-size sensitivity, learned versus reparameterized score/velocity comparisons, stochasticity analyses, independently varied score/velocity training checkpoints, and detailed hyperparameter sweeps (Figures 9–10, 12–13, 16; Table 9). These substantially expand testing of numerical reliability beyond v1's retained overlap and ratio-magnitude analyses.

E5.justification: V2 newly specifies three training replicates for the detailed Gaussian schedule sweep in Table 9. Existing Gaussian summaries retain five-run reporting, while MI and differential-abundance tables retain three-run mean ± standard error reporting. No increase in runs for the retained headline results is established.

E6.justification: Table 1 changes throughout: at dimension 320, TSM changes from 28.85 ± 1.20 to 3.55 ± 0.12, while scRatio with lambda 0.25 changes from 0.46 ± 0.15 to 1.16 ± 0.27. ScRatio's reported ranking changes from three dimension-wise wins to four wins and one tie. These are revised results under changed reference values and baseline tuning, alongside substantial new classifier and ablation results.

T1.justification: V2 adds Proposition 4.2's KL-based lower bound on cumulative squared log-ratio variation and its proof in B.9. Appendix B.8 adds general and Gaussian-specific first-order approximation-error analyses with proofs. Proposition 4.1 also gains an explicit shared-support assumption; the original ratio dynamics remain.

C1.justification: The four principal contributions remain. However, the abstract, introduction, and discussion now explicitly emphasize compounded discretization errors, and the discussion claims that avoiding separate integrations reduces these errors and improves estimation quality.

C2.justification: V2 substantially expands explanations of simulation-field choice, dimensional amplification of approximation errors, classifier saturation, and the relative importance of velocity and score accuracy. It retains the low-overlap limitation but adds proposed failure diagnostics using ratio histograms and pulled-back noise (C.4), plus an adaptive-solver explanation for decreasing runtime.

D1.justification: V2 identifies the dopri5 solver and documents baseline tuning grids and new ablation settings. Conversely, it removes v1's explicit 50% condition-drop frequency for MI training. The architecture descriptions, existing hyperparameter tables, and code-access link are retained.

R1.justification: New Appendix C.3 substantially expands positioning against classifier-based, kernel/moment-matching, and time-score estimators, including the distinction that conditional flows permit comparisons without pair-specific retraining. V2 also adds Chen et al. (2026), Kompot, and a KLIEP-related citation. Publication updates to retained references do not constitute new works.

P1.justification: V2 refines prose and terminology, streamlines Section 4's use-case equations, moves the explicit S1 integral into B.7, and inserts explanatory subsections. The main section sequence and experimental narrative remain recognizable. Affiliations and the publication header are also updated.

P2.justification: V2 adds substantial visual material: sample-size and reparameterization plots, stochasticity and hyperparameter boxplots, training-checkpoint heatmaps, and Table 9. Figure 8 gains classifier-comparison panels, and Table 1 gains a classifier row. Existing figures are resized or reformatted, with expanded captions and relocated appendix displays.

improvement.justification: The new reparameterization and score/velocity ablations directly test design choices that v1 largely justified verbally, while baseline tuning strengthens the comparisons. These provide a limited net improvement. The gain is tempered by replacing analytic MI targets with coarse rounded values, which weakens that accuracy benchmark and prevents interpreting Table 1's revisions as same-setting performance gains.
